Read animal and tag records from an OTN, GLATOS or detqc sheet

Source: R/read_animals.R
read_animals.Rd

Reads tagging records into the contract's animals and tags table, one row per animal and transmitter. It reads the OTN tagging sheet (Excel, header row found by its names), the OTN AAT tag release file, the tagging sheet of a GLATOS project workbook, and GLATOS detection exports, whose animal columns repeat on every row and are reduced to one row per animal and transmitter. A transmitter reused on a second animal keeps one row per animal, with a warning that names it; detset() then gives each detection to the animal released last before it. A GLATOS workbook's release times are local, in glatos_release_date_time at the zone in glatos_timezone; where utc_release_date_time is blank they are converted to UTC.

Usage

read_animals(
  file,
  format = c("auto", "otn", "glatos", "detqc"),
  col_map = NULL,
  tz = NULL,
  tag_specs = NULL,
  missing_id = c("drop", "transmitter")
)

Arguments

file

Path to a CSV or Excel file.

format

One of "auto", "otn", "glatos" or "detqc".

col_map

Optional column map. A data frame, or the path to a CSV file, laid out as column_map() describes, replaces the packaged map. Pairs written as c(target = "source") are merged into the format's map: each replaces the rows of its target, and the other targets are read as the format reads them. A pair whose column is not in the file stops; column_map() gives the order in which a pair names the columns the format joins, as GLATOS joins two for transmitter.

tz

Optional time zone, from OlsonNames(), for stamps that carry no zone of their own. NULL uses the zone in the column map (UTC for every packaged format).

tag_specs

Optional result of read_tag_specs(), or a data frame with transmitter and tag_serial: the codes of each tag serial.

missing_id

"drop" (default) drops rows with no animal_id; "transmitter" names such an animal by its transmitter.

Value

A data frame, one row per animal and transmitter, with animal_id and transmitter and, where the sheet gives them, species, release_datetime (UTC), release_lat, release_lon, tag_model, tag_serial, tag_life_days, min_delay and max_delay

(s), sensor_type, sensor_unit, sensor_slope and sensor_intercept, then any other mapped column such as length. The OTN tagging template states length in metres and weight in kilograms, so for format = "otn" the units are added as length_unit

("m") and weight_unit ("kg") where the sheet has those columns, and the review cards print them. The GLATOS workbook names no unit for LENGTH or WEIGHT, so for format = "glatos" no unit column is added and the cards print the value with "(unit as recorded)".

Details

Format. "auto" takes the OTN or GLATOS map, whichever fills more of the contract columns from the file's columns, and OTN on a tie, as read_deployments() does; a warning names a contract column the other format would fill and the chosen one leaves empty, such as release_datetime of a GLATOS workbook read with format = "otn". Where that column is one the table needs, such as transmitter of a GLATOS detection export read with format = "otn", the reader stops and names the format "auto" picks. A format other than the four stops with the formats listed. A file with detqc's own column names, such as a detset's animals written with write.csv(), fills the most contract columns and is read as "detqc". A blank-headed first column of unique whole numbers, the row names write.csv() writes by default, is dropped.

OTN tagging sheets and detection extracts. The OTN tagging template often leaves ANIMAL_ID blank, while the OTN matched extract names each animal by its catalogNumber. Read such a sheet with missing_id = "transmitter": detset() then warns that the extract's animal_id disagrees with the animals table, and filter_release(), filter_post_release() and filter_tag_life() take the release of a detection whose animal_id the animals table does not list by its transmitter, with a message that counts them.

Rows with no animal or no transmitter. A row needs both. Rows that lack one are dropped with a warning that counts each cause apart and names an example, and the attribute source keeps the counts (dropped_no_animal_id, dropped_no_transmitter). In an OTN sheet a blank TAG_CODE_SPACE leaves the transmitter blank though the animal has an id. With tag_specs, such a row takes its transmitters from the tag specifications by tag_serial. A GLATOS detection export can leave animal_id blank on every row; missing_id = "transmitter" then names each animal by its transmitter, as glatos does. When every row would be dropped, read_animals() stops. It stops too when more than half the rows have no animal_id, with an error that names the columns it read the id from, or no transmitter after tag_specs has filled what it can, with an error that names the blank code space. Exactly half is a warning.

Tags that send two codes. A tag with a pinger and a sensor, or two sensors, sends two transmitter codes, and tagging sheets often list one. With tag_specs, every code the specifications list for an animal's tag_serial gets its own row on that animal, with the tag columns of the specifications. The second codes can carry a large share of an animal's detections.

Tag columns from the specifications. Sensor calibrations and transmission delays are not in the tagging sheets. They are in the manufacturer's tag specification sheet, which read_tag_specs() reads. With tag_specs, every row whose transmitter the specifications list takes their tag columns (tag_model, tag_life_days, min_delay, max_delay, sensor_type, sensor_unit, sensor_slope and sensor_intercept) where its own value is missing; the codes the sheet lists and the second codes added from the specifications then agree. A value the sheet gives is kept; where it differs from the specifications, a warning counts the cells by column and names one. Tag serials of the sheet that the specifications do not list get a warning too, sensor tags first: such a tag loses its second code and its calibration, so find its vendor sheet. A code the sheet gives for a serial whose specifications list other codes, such as A69-9002-13710 where the specifications list A69-9007-13710 for the same serial, is most often a slip in the sheet's code space. It is kept beside the specifications' codes, and a warning names each such pair, so that the slip can be checked against the detections and dropped. The attribute source counts the cells filled (spec_cells_filled), the differing cells (spec_conflicts), the serials not listed (serials_not_in_specs) and the sheet codes not listed for their serial (codes_not_in_specs).

Examples

csv_file <- system.file("extdata", "stoney_detections.csv", package = "detqc")
animals <- read_animals(csv_file, format = "glatos")
animals[, c("animal_id", "transmitter", "species", "release_datetime")]
#>   animal_id    transmitter species    release_datetime
#> 1     ST-02 A69-9002-61002 walleye 2024-06-02 15:30:00
#> 2     ST-04 A69-1601-61004 walleye 2024-06-02 15:30:00
#> 3     ST-03 A69-9002-61003 walleye 2024-06-02 15:30:00
#> 4     ST-01 A69-1601-61001 walleye 2024-06-02 15:30:00
